data.narrative:
Ouster is a publicly traded semiconductor company founded by Angus Pacala with a current valuation of $2.26B and total capital raised exceeding $500M. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public-stage peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, alongside 8 additional private frontier-tech companies in the same vertical.

The peer-median method was the applicable triangulation approach. Using Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B) as same-sector, same-stage benchmarks, the median valuation is $35.8B with a full range spanning $1.1B to $39.2B. Public-comp anchoring using sector price-to-sales multiples (20.5x median across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD) could not be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure, typical for private-stage peer analysis. The single-method triangulation inherently constrains precision.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30.4B (low) to $41.2B (high), with a median of $35.8B. Material uncertainty stems from the wide dispersion within the peer set—Aeva trades at a substantial discount relative to Cerebras—and the absence of revenue-based valuation anchors. The current $2.26B valuation sits materially below the peer-median benchmark, suggesting either differentiated risk profile, earlier commercial stage, or distinct market positioning relative to comparable public companies.
